title: Hero hooks & signal matrix for homepage/product pages
body:
Purpose: quick iteration doc for homepage and product-page hero copy + a compact signal matrix to pick variant priorities. This is a working playbook — not final. Use this to seed experiments and hand off to growth and design for flows and CTAs.

Context notes (short): Redwood's differentiation for developers is production-grade inference economics: predictable latency, cost controls, and operational safety across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. We want hero copy that: 1) resonates with engineers and platform teams, 2) communicates measurable benefits (latency/cost/availability), and 3) surfaces the multi-environment consistency promise.

Audience segments (prioritized):
- Developer / engineering-first (fast prototyping, low cognitive friction)
- Platform / infra teams (SRE, reliability guarantees, observability)
- Product teams at mid-market / enterprise (SLA, security, VPC/on-prem)

Signal matrix (how we judge hero variants):
- Signal: Developer resonance (qualitative feedback + click-through to quickstart)
- Signal: Trust & enterprise readiness (trial sign-ups with company email, demo requests)
- Signal: Cost-metric comprehension (engagement with cost explainer page or calculator)
- Signal: Latency conviction (time-to-first-token and latency graphs viewed)
- Signal: Activation (API keys created and first inference call within 48h)

Priority weighting: Developer resonance 30%, Activation 25%, Trust 20%, Cost comprehension 15%, Latency conviction 10%.

Hero variants (short, each with one-line subhead + primary CTA suggestion):
1) "Predictable inference, anywhere you run it." | Subhead: "Same API, same SLAs — hosted, dedicated, or in your VPC." | CTA: Try the API (free credits)
2) "Serve models with enterprise-grade predictability." | Subhead: "Latency SLOs, fallbacks, and routing policies built in." | CTA: Request demo
3) "Low-latency model serving that scales with your app." | Subhead: "Continuous batching, KV caching, and smart routing for stable p99s." | CTA: See benchmarks
4) "Make inference costs predictable, not mysterious." | Subhead: "Batched execution, quantization suggestions, and per-token breakdowns." | CTA: Cost calculator
5) "One runtime. Any deployment. Fewer surprises." | Subhead: "Unify hosted, dedicated, and private deployments under one API." | CTA: Compare deployments
6) "Ship LLM features without operating the stack." | Subhead: "From live chat to embeddings — production controls included." | CTA: Quickstart guide
7) "Trustworthy inference: fallbacks and audits by default." | Subhead: "Automatic fallbacks, audit logs, KMS-ready keying." | CTA: Security brief
8) "Optimize latency and cost — automatically." | Subhead: "Adaptive batching, cache reuse, and model selection suggestions." | CTA: Optimization report
9) "The developer-first inference runtime." | Subhead: "SDKs, streaming, function calls, and clear performance profiles." | CTA: Developer docs
10) "Predictable inference economics for product teams." | Subhead: "Unit economics surfaced per-route and per-model." | CTA: Pricing examples

Notes on tone and voice:
- Primary voice: pragmatic, engineering-respectful, numbers-forward. Avoid fluffy statements about "AI magic"; prefer measurable claims (ms, p99, % cost reduction).
- Secondary voice for enterprise pages: formal, security-aware, SLA-first.
- Microcopy: use concrete verbs (deploy, route, rollback), use consistent nouns (inference, model, deployment).

Product page header suggestions (distinct for each product):
- Hosted API header: "Turnkey inference API — start in minutes." Subhead: "Curated models, streaming, and predictable developer experience."
- Dedicated header: "Reserved GPU capacity for production throughput." Subhead: "Configurable autoscale, burst options, and SLA-backed latency."
- Private header: "Private control plane for regulated workloads." Subhead: "VPC or on-prem deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, audit trails."

Competitive differentiation bullets to surface on product pages (short):
- Unified API across environments (avoid re-architecture at scale)
- Observable unit economics (per-token and per-route breakdowns)
- Automatic fallbacks and model variant routing (resilience without manual playbooks)
- Smart batching + cache reuse to cut unit cost while preserving p99s
- Enterprise-first networking and key management options

Competitor notes (working brainstorm):
- Many vendors pitch "easy hosting" or "model zoo"; our angle: operational certainty and economics, not just access to models.
- Watch for competitors emphasizing feature parity (tooling) — double-down on numbers and reproducible benchmarks.
- For messaging, avoid naming competitors; call them generically (cloud endpoints, managed model APIs, open runtime stacks).

Experiment matrix (concrete):
- A/B test group A: Variant 1, CTA "Try the API" leading to quickstart with a 3-step guide.
- A/B test group B: Variant 4, CTA "Cost calculator" leading to a short interactive calculator.
- Secondary funnel test: For enterprise traffic, show Variant 2 with secondary CTA to "Request SLA info".
- Measurement window: 14 days per test, target 1000 qualified visits per variant or 3,000 total visits.

KPIs to monitor per variant: CTR to primary CTA, time-to-api-key (median), API activation within 48h, demo requests per 1k visits, bounce rate on cost pages.

Content experiments (ideas for copy packs):
- Numbered proof points under hero (3 bullets): e.g., "p99 80–120ms on standard scenarios; 30% median cost saving via batching; SLA-backed uptime." Use real internal numbers from benchmarks when available.
- Developer snippet under hero: 1-line curl + sample response and a token cost estimate to reduce friction.
- Quick toggles in hero for audience: "For devs | For platform | For security" that swap subhead + CTA.

Design/UX constraints and notes:
- Hero must render above the fold with a succinct claim + one supporting metric. Mobile-first: keep claim short; push subhead below.
- Avoid excessive jargon on above-the-fold; use jargon in secondary content for technical readers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Get exact p99 numbers from serving-runtime benchmarks and decide which are safe to publish (action: @engineering/serving-runtime to provide a sanitized benchmark snapshot).
- Confirm pricing example buckets with finance for the "pricing examples" CTA (action: @finance).
- Build the interactive cost calculator (hand off to growth/UX).

Appendix: sample long-form hero for product page (two-paragraph draft) — copy to be used in case we run a landing with more context: 
"Redwood Inference gives teams the predictability to ship LLM features at scale. Across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments, you get consistent latency SLOs, routing policies, and transparent per-route economics — so product teams can plan capacity and finance can forecast spend.

Under the hood, we optimize inference with continuous batching, KV caching, and automatic model variant fallbacks to reduce cost without surprising your SLAs. Ship faster: same API surface across environments, built-in observability, and enterprise controls when you need them."

Contact notes: feedback welcome in #gtm-hero-copy. We'll sync with design on Friday 2025-02-21 to mock top 3 variants.

Quick filenames for export: hero-hooks-signal-matrix.json (this doc), hero-assets/variant-pack-1.md (design deliverable), experiments/GTMP-412-a.json (A/B test config).

End of working doc.
